custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Have three active parts: part A and part B in category A, and part C in category B, so the category A filter leaves part C out.
  • Give parts A, B and C part numbers that start with the same text, so one search lists all three.
  • Use a longer search text that still matches all three part numbers.
  • Start on the Inventory page (Parts in the top bar, then Inventory in the left menu), on the Active tab.

How to set this up on the QA site (https://sv10647.qa.shopview.com):

  • Admin at the test location: on the QA site's sign-in screen choose Admin. The test location is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919; its name shows in the box at the top right. If another name shows, click that box, click the name beside Change Location: and pick Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • To create a part: click Parts in the top bar, Inventory in the left menu, then New Inventory Part. Fill Description and Part Number (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-C425598-A for part A, -B for part B), pick a Category, type a Cost and a Sell Price, type the Quantity in the bin row (the location's bin, for example General Storage, is offered), then click Save. Leave Track quantities and cost of goods on for a tracked part; click it off for an untracked part. Add Bin Location adds a second bin; Vendor, Manufacturer, Core Charge, Min, Max and Tags are in the same window. Parts that must start with the same text all start ZZAUTOTEST-PL-C425598-, so searching for that finds them all.
  • The Search box above the Inventory list opens when you click Search (the magnifier).
  • Theme: click your avatar (the AS circle) at the top right; Light and Dark are at the bottom of its menu.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Parts A, B and C are listed.

Step 2:

  • The menu opens.

Step 3:

  • Bulk mode turns on.

Step 4:

  • The part A row is ticked.

Step 5:

  • The bar reads 2 selected.

Step 6:

  • The order of the rows changes, and parts A and B stay ticked: the bar still reads 2 selected.

Step 7:

  • The order reverses, and the bar still reads 2 selected.

Step 8:

  • Parts A, B and C are still listed, but the ticks are cleared: no row is ticked and the bar reads 0 selected.

Step 9:

  • The part A row is ticked.

Step 10:

  • The bar reads 2 selected again.

Step 11:

  • Only parts A and B are listed, and the ticks are cleared: the bar reads 0 selected.

Step 12:

  • Bulk mode ends and no part changed status.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10815 (Story 2, Deactivate Parts in Bulk)

  • S2-R10a: “Changing the search term or a filter clears the ticks, so the user only ever changes parts they can see. Sorting keeps them.”
